I just thought I'd share two of my favorite things I've ever learned with you guys, both of which are breathing exercises that have an unbelievably powerful effect on your mental and physical state. One is very much a stimulating, "upper" technique, and the other is a beautifully relaxing, "downer" technique. I'll explain them both now so that you can try them for yourselves.

4-7-8 method [relaxing]- it's pretty simple. You start by exhaling, emptying your lungs completely. You then breathe in through your nose, filling up your lungs to a count of four. Now hold the breath in for a count of seven, and finally, breathe out through your mouth [which should be in an O shape] for a count of eight, making an exhaling noise while you do so. Repeat four times. I like to do it by a clock and use the ticking to count so I can focus on the breathing. This technique has a very strong soothing effect and is great to do when you want to relax, or when you're feeling very anxious about an upcoming event.

12-cycle meth breath [stimulating]- don't let the name put you off, it's just what the goofy book I read about it in called it, and I can't think of anything better. It's done by taking four sharp inhales and exhales lasting only a second each with as little pause inbetween them as possible, then on the fifth breath, taking a very powerful eight second inhale, and a very complete ten second exhale. This completes one cycle. Do it twelve times and you're done, and you'll be feeling energetic in a more positive way than any energy supplement you'll ever try. Theoretically you can do it more than twelve times for greater effect, but I've never needed it and I wouldn't recommend it. This exercise would be great to do when you're feeling demotivated, or with or in place of a cup of coffee to get you pumped.before your workout. I wouldn't recommend doing it more than once a day though, as it starts to lose it's effect if you do, in my experience.

There you have it, two wonderful exercises. Now just pick one and try it, depending on how you'd like to feel at the moment. I think you'll be quite pleased with the results. I was practically giddy the first time I tried each of these, although I guess I'm just an excitable person. Nevertheless, I think these techniques will be quite helpful to you too, and once you master them, they'll even help you control your emotional state on an ongoing basis.

I love breathing exercises! They make me feel like an old-timey Strongman. I personally like vacuum holds, where, on an empty stomach, you suck in your gut as hard as you can (imagine sticking the inside of your stomach to your spine), and hold it there for about 30 seconds. I'm not sure how exactly you're supposed to breathe without sacrificing form, but it helps manage my beer gut.

The important thing about breath exercises is to breathe more through your abdomen. If you take a deep breath and your shoulders rise considerably, you're doing it wrong. Don't breathe through your chest, it has way less capacity than your abdomen. It may feel weird at first, but after a while you'll wonder how you ever managed to screw up something as simple as breathing.
